root_idea.summary: The central orientation is the earth or ground: what is below and opposite the sky, including the terrestrial surface and what rests upon it.
root_idea.development: From this basic notion, the lexicon develops descriptions of fertile, soft, productive land, lower parts, remaining fixed to the ground, and figurative submissiveness. Rheum and tremor are reported as separate, non-analogical lexical branches.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The single QAC group is the Quran-attested noun أرض; it is displayed under its normalized classical citation form.

senses.definition: The earth, ground, or land; the terrestrial expanse or a tract of country.
senses.usage_conditions: The noun may refer to the earth as opposed to heaven, to its surface or soil, or to an inhabited or cultivated land. In the expression “the earth after its death,” the physical image is extended to renewal after corruption and return after an initial state; it is also interpreted figuratively as the softening of hearts after hardness.

senses.definition: In دَابَّةُ الأَرْضِ, the earth-creature, identified in this Quranic attestation as a wood-eating insect.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a conventional Quranic expression; the identification of the creature as the insect that consumed Solomon’s staff belongs to the lexical explanation of the expression, not to a general standalone meaning of أرض.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of land: to become thriving, fertile, productive, soft, moisture-retaining, and rich in herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verbal use describing the condition of land or pasture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a person: to become lowly or submissive and naturally disposed to good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form I use applied to a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To find land abundant in herbage or pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I transitive use with the land as the object of finding or judging.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of wood: to be eaten by the wood-fretter or termite.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive verbal construction describing damage caused by أَرَضَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an ulcer or sore: to become blistered, widened, corrupt with thick matter, and split open.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verbal use for a deteriorating sore.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be affected by rheum or a cold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Two reported vocalizations occur in this verbal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To graze the herbage of the earth and seek after it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II use; the related verbal noun may describe grazing or searching for pasture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek out or choose a place for alighting or abiding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional use with a place of lodging or settlement as the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make heavy, slow, or sluggish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported Form II causative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone tarry, wait, or remain patient in expectation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported extension of the Form II use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a place or land: to be abundant in herbage, level or soft, productive, and good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV use, often appearing in an exclamation about the quality of a place or land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to be affected by rheum.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV causative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of herbage: to reach a state in which it can be cut.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V use describing mature or harvestable vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cling to the ground, remain fixed in a place, or tarry there in expectation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may describe staying at a place without leaving, waiting, or pausing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become heavy, slow, or sluggish, inclining toward the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V bodily or behavioral description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To approach someone asking or petitioning for something desired.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed idiomatic use, synonymous with presenting oneself or humbly supplicating.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of clouds: to expand or spread, or according to another report, to become fixed or stationary.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X use applied to clouds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ground-like submissiveness, endurance, or lack of resistance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative idiom compares a submissive or uncomplaining person to ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stranger whose father and mother are unknown.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed compound expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A low-growing plant found on hilltops, eaten as a herb and quick to dry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plant name in the compound ابن الأرض; related plural expressions may denote plants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In compound expressions, concealed places, pools left by torrents, pools retaining water, or rivulets.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are specialized compound uses rather than a general standalone sense of أرض.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A carpet or anything spread out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use; in poetry this usage may be treated grammatically as masculine.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Anything low or the lower part next to the ground, including the lower legs of an animal, a man’s knees and what lies below them, or the underside of a sandal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The specific application depends on the object: animal legs, a person’s lower limbs, or the part of a sole touching the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A febrile shivering, tremor, or vertigo.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a separate lexical branch from أرض meaning earth; the tremor may be associated with a relaxed state and discharge from the nose and eyes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rheum or a cold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This nominal use is masculine in the cited report and is distinct from the earth noun in meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A class of jinn believed to possess people and cause involuntary trembling or movement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized compound expression associated with the tremor sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Herbage sufficient for camels or other grazing animals for a year; abundant pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized pasture noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The wood-fretter or termite, an insect that eats wood and may damage plants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun can be collective in use; the insect is described as a white worm or winged termite in different reports.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of land: fertile, productive, pleasing, soft or level, moisture-retaining, and rich in vegetation; also, broadly, wide.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival branch describing the quality or breadth of land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wide or fat as an epithet, including a broad or fat person or animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form may occur as an imitative counterpart of عريض and can describe a kid or a woman; the examples do not impose an object-class restriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lowly, submissive, or naturally disposed to good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use applied to a person or character.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The most adapted, suitable, fit, or worthy among them for a thing or action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed superlative-like expression with a following object or action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wood eaten by the wood-fretter or termite.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial description of wood damaged by the insect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person affected by a disorder attributed to jinn and moving the head or body involuntarily.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized passive participle associated with the tremor or possession branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person affected by rheum or a cold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized passive participial use; the reported morphology varies in relation to the causative verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a young palm: having established a root in the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X participial use for a young palm or offshoot rooted in the soil.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Heavy, slow, or sluggish, inclining toward the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized adjectival or participial use.
